source_notes.note: Construction and terminology were checked against published beginner patterns and Craft Yarn Council terminology. The learner-facing wording below is original.

materials.detail: 4.0 mm (US G/6) is a starting point; adjust for yarn

stitch_glossary.name: Magic Ring
stitch_glossary.description: An adjustable loop used to begin crocheting in the round.

stitch_glossary.name: Chain
stitch_glossary.description: Yarn over and pull the yarn through the loop on the hook.

stitch_glossary.name: Slip Stitch
stitch_glossary.description: Insert the hook, yarn over, and pull the yarn through the stitch and the loop on the hook.

stitch_glossary.name: Single Crochet
stitch_glossary.description: Insert the hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through both loops.

stitch_glossary.name: Half Double Crochet
stitch_glossary.description: Yarn over, insert the hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through all three loops.

stitch_glossary.name: Double Crochet
stitch_glossary.description: Yarn over, insert the hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then work off the loops two at a time.

steps.name: Create the center ring
steps.instruction: Make a magic ring. Keep the adjustable loop loose enough to work stitches into it.
steps.expected_result: You should have a small adjustable loop ready for the first round.
common_mistakes: Making the ring too tight to insert the hook.
Confusing the yarn tail with the working yarn.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is starting a magic ring and may need help identifying the working yarn and keeping the ring open.

steps.name: Work 10 single crochets
steps.instruction: Chain 1; this does not count as a stitch. Work 10 single crochet stitches into the magic ring.
steps.expected_result: Ten single crochet stitches should sit around the center ring.
common_mistakes: Counting the chain-1 as a stitch.
Working outside the ring instead of through the ring.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner needs to maintain a count of 10 single crochets and understand where the hook enters the magic ring.

steps.name: Close and join the center
steps.instruction: Pull the yarn tail gently to close the center. Join with a slip stitch to the first single crochet.
steps.expected_result: The center should be closed with a neat circular base and no large hole.
common_mistakes: Pulling the tail before all stitches are complete.
Joining into the chain-1 instead of the first single crochet.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner may be unsure which stitch is the first single crochet or how tightly to close the magic ring.

steps.name: Create five petal spaces
steps.instruction: Chain 3, skip the next stitch, and slip stitch into the following stitch. Repeat this sequence around the circle until you have 5 chain-3 spaces.
steps.expected_result: Five evenly spaced chain-3 loops should form around the center.
common_mistakes: Putting the slip stitch into the wrong stitch.
Losing count of the five spaces.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is creating the five spaces that will hold the petals and may need help identifying a chain space.

steps.name: Build the petals
steps.instruction: Work into each chain-3 space, not into the stitches underneath it. In each space make: 1 sc, 1 hdc, 3 dc, 1 hdc, 1 sc. Repeat for all 5 spaces.
steps.expected_result: Each chain-3 space should become one rounded petal, giving the flower five petals.
common_mistakes: Working into the center stitches instead of the chain space.
Missing one of the three double crochets.
Making petals with different stitch sequences.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is forming petals and may need help understanding that all five stitches groups are worked into the chain-3 spaces.

steps.name: Fasten off and finish
steps.instruction: Fasten off, leaving a short yarn tail. Use a tapestry needle to weave the ends securely into the back of the flower. Gently shape the petals.
steps.expected_result: The flower should hold its shape with secure ends hidden on the back.
common_mistakes: Cutting the yarn too close to the work.
Leaving the ends unsecured.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is finishing the flower and may need guidance on weaving in ends and shaping petals.

source_notes.note: The references validate the beginner amigurumi structure and use of magic ring, single crochet, increases, decreases, stuffing and assembly. The simplified learner pattern below is original and is not a reproduction of either source.

materials.detail: Cotton or acrylic yarn suitable for a 3–3.5 mm hook
For sewing and weaving in ends
Use embroidery instead of safety eyes for very young children
materials.quantity: 2 eyes or small amount of thread

stitch_glossary.name: Magic Ring
stitch_glossary.description: An adjustable loop used to begin working in the round.

stitch_glossary.name: Single Crochet
stitch_glossary.description: The basic compact stitch used for the bunny body.

stitch_glossary.name: Increase
stitch_glossary.description: Work two single crochets into the same stitch to increase the stitch count by one.

stitch_glossary.name: Decrease
stitch_glossary.description: Combine two stitches into one to reduce the stitch count.

stitch_glossary.name: Slip Stitch
stitch_glossary.description: A low-profile stitch used for joining or finishing.

steps.name: Start the head
steps.instruction: Make a magic ring and work 6 single crochets into it. Close the ring.
steps.expected_result: A tiny closed circle forms the center of the head.
common_mistakes: Losing the stitch count.
Pulling the ring so tightly that the hook cannot enter the stitches.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is beginning an amigurumi-style piece and needs help maintaining a tight, compact center.

steps.name: Increase the head
steps.instruction: Work an increase in every stitch of the previous round, giving you 12 single crochet stitches.
steps.expected_result: The circle should widen evenly without large gaps.
common_mistakes: Putting only one stitch into an increase point.
Adding increases randomly and creating an uneven shape.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner needs to understand that an increase means two single crochets in the same base stitch.

steps.name: Build the head
steps.instruction: Work 3 rounds of 12 single crochets, keeping the stitch count constant.
steps.expected_result: The piece begins to form a small rounded tube.
common_mistakes: Accidentally increasing or decreasing.
Losing the beginning of the round.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is working continuous rounds and may need help using a stitch marker to track the round start.

steps.name: Shape the head
steps.instruction: Work one decrease at every third stitch around the round, then continue single crochet rounds until the opening is small enough to add stuffing.
steps.expected_result: The top should begin narrowing into a rounded head.
common_mistakes: Decreasing too many times in one round.
Overstuffing before the opening is ready.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is shaping a rounded amigurumi form using decreases and may need help understanding why the stitch count gets smaller.

steps.name: Stuff and close
steps.instruction: Add small amounts of stuffing until the head is firm but not stretched. Continue decreasing around the opening until it closes. Fasten off.
steps.expected_result: A firm rounded head with a closed bottom.
common_mistakes: Overstuffing and stretching the stitches.
Leaving a large opening at the end.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner needs help judging stuffing density and closing an amigurumi opening neatly.

steps.name: Make the ears
steps.instruction: Make two small ear pieces using a short chain and single crochet stitches worked along the chain. Fasten off each ear and leave a sewing tail.
common_mistakes: Making the ears different lengths.
Forgetting to leave a sewing tail.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is making separate flat pieces and may need help keeping both ears the same size.

steps.name: Assemble the bunny
steps.instruction: Position the two ears symmetrically on top of the head and sew them securely with the yarn tails. Add eyes using safety eyes or embroidery thread.
steps.expected_result: The finished piece should clearly resemble a small bunny.
common_mistakes: Sewing the ears at different heights.
Leaving loose ends after assembly.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is assembling the bunny and needs guidance on symmetry and secure finishing.

projects.title: Simple Single-Crochet Coaster
projects.finished_size: Approximately 4 inches square, depending on tension

source_notes.note: Beginner coaster references validate the project type and foundational techniques. The square single-crochet stitch counts below are an original simplified learning pattern.

materials.detail: 100% cotton is recommended for a practical coaster
5.0 mm starting point; adjust to yarn and tension
For weaving in the final ends

stitch_glossary.name: Slip Knot
stitch_glossary.description: A starting knot that creates the adjustable loop placed on the hook.

stitch_glossary.name: Chain
stitch_glossary.description: Yarn over and pull through the loop on the hook.

stitch_glossary.name: Single Crochet
stitch_glossary.description: Insert the hook, yarn over and pull up a loop, then yarn over and pull through both loops.

steps.name: Make the foundation chain
steps.instruction: Make a slip knot and chain 21 stitches.
steps.expected_result: A foundation chain with 21 chain stitches.
common_mistakes: Making the chain too tight to insert the hook.
Accidentally counting the slip knot as a chain.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is creating the foundation chain and may need help keeping chain tension even.

steps.name: Work the first row
steps.instruction: Insert the hook into the second chain from the hook and make 1 single crochet. Continue with 1 single crochet in each remaining chain.
steps.expected_result: The first row contains 20 single crochet stitches.
common_mistakes: Crocheting into the first loop on the hook.
Skipping a chain while working across.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner needs to understand the second-chain starting point and keep a 20-stitch row count.

steps.name: Turn and begin the next row
steps.instruction: Chain 1, turn your work, and make 1 single crochet in each stitch across the row.
steps.expected_result: The second row should have the same 20-stitch width as the first.
common_mistakes: Forgetting to turn the work.
Missing the first or last stitch of the row.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is moving from a foundation chain to repeated rows and may lose the edge stitches.

steps.name: Repeat the rows
steps.instruction: Continue repeating Step 3 until you have 20 rows total. Count each completed row to keep the coaster square.
steps.expected_result: The piece should gradually form a square with 20 stitches across and 20 rows.
common_mistakes: Ending with fewer or more than 20 rows.
Dropping an edge stitch and making the coaster narrower.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is repeating rows and needs help counting rows and recognizing when an edge stitch has been missed.

steps.name: Fasten off
steps.instruction: After the 20th row, cut the yarn leaving a tail, pull the tail through the final loop, and tighten gently.
steps.expected_result: The final stitch is secured and the coaster will not unravel.
common_mistakes: Cutting the tail too short.
Pulling the final loop too loosely.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is finishing the project and needs to secure the final loop before weaving in the end.

steps.name: Weave in the ends
steps.instruction: Use a tapestry needle to weave the starting and ending yarn tails through several stitches on the back of the coaster. Trim the excess yarn.
steps.expected_result: No loose yarn tails remain visible on the finished coaster.
common_mistakes: Weaving too little yarn.
Cutting the yarn before it is securely woven.
steps.ai_help_context: The learner is finishing the coaster and may need a simple explanation of how to hide yarn tails safely.
